doc.title: Ruthie Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 28, 2023

title: Mahalia Jackson
summary: Foster grew up on Mahalia Jackson and values her power and physical singing.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Aw. That’s lovely. A couple more things and I’ll wrap up, this has just been marvelous. I wanted to run a couple of names by you and just see how they — what they might elicit. Mahalia Jackson?

Powerful. Nothing but power. Absolutely. I grew up listening to a lot of Mahalia, and still do. Still do. To remind myself when you sing remember where that comes from and not just spirit-wise but even physically. You’re listening to her sing and she’s a very physical singer. As a vocalist or just as a musician who’s knowledgeable about that and the physics of when it comes to how you use your body, you see and you feel that with Mahalia. You know where it’s coming from.
